title: Directing the Four Blazers' act at the Pearl Theater in Philadelphia
summary: The 1931 band played the week Ellington was off; Randolph worked out the tempos for the Four Blazers but misjudged the tempo at the performance.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: You know, it's a funny thing. Talking about the -- this young Porter band. But I would like to go back to '31 when we played this Pearl Theater.
Which? Pearl Theater?
Pearl Theater, in '31.
Is that in Baltimore?
That's in Philadelphia.
Philadelphia.
Yes. And here's -- we had on the bill a dance team called the Four Blazers. That was formerly with Duke Ellington's band. Well, Duke played that week, so they
held the Four Blazers over because Duke was off. Duke laid off a week. And when Duke laid off a week, we came in and we played the Pearl Theater that week the Duke was off. This was back into '31.
Yes.

So I had to do the directing of the band and arrange the show and so forth. So the Four Blazers, they passed the music out. When they passed the music out, they come and they looked at the band. I guess it was kind of a letdown for them to see such a small band, after --
Yeah, after Ellington.
-- leaving Ellington's band, and a hardhitting band like that, you know.
Yeah.

And he says, well, he picked out the pieces and he had some music (unintelligible), okay, I looked the music over, I says to the band, I says, go to letter F. And the boys would go to F, and I said, look out, one -- counted it down, one, two, three, four. The band started to playing tempo goes letter F. Gosh, we got tempo (unintelligible) just like that. I said, (inaudible)please wait a minute. So we're looking it over now.
So I wiped that part out. Okay, and I kept working it out, and I knew the guys was going to get stumped on, you know, and I'd work them out. So finally after I got all those

little modulations, all those little trick parts worked out, then, I said, now, how do you guys feel about this thing? You ready to take it down now? They said, yeah, say, Randolph, we're ready now. I said, okay.

So I went across to the Four Blazers and I said, now, give me your tempo. So he gave me the tempo. He gave me the tempo, so we hit it, we carried it down, they danced, he said everything was okay. Thanks, thanks, man, yeah, that's okay, that's all right. Thank you, man, thanks.
Well, that night of the performance, I misjudged the tempo.
Oh, no.
And picked the tempo up.
Uh-huh.
I picked the tempo up, and -- look out, one, one, two, three, four. And the bandleader jumped, and all the guys went on down.
When we finished, those guys said, 'oh, 'fess' (inaudible), pull that tempo down a little bit, will you?
Yeah, dancers are --
Yeah, those things was really funny.

Well, it show you, though, if you really don't know how to handle the situations when they arise, why, a person can make a fool out of you up there. But you really got to know it, you got to know what you're doing when you're up there.
That's when the way your playing shows.
You can't just use this for a hatrack.
That's right.
Yes, sir.
